title: agent-sandbox state.json
description: Authoritative shape for state.json. Skills 1, 2, and 3 all read this file; field names pinned here so skills can't drift.

schema_version.description: Accepts 1 or 2 so a v1 file validates before it is migrated in memory to 2. Code hard-fails anything > 2 (skill too old). The github[]/mongodb[] arrays are required only at version 2 (see the top-level allOf).

username.description: whoami of the user at init time. Used in sudoers, ACL, paths.

macos_user.description: Hardcoded for v1. Future-proofing: leaving it in state.json so a future migration can rename without breaking older skill installs.

default_account_id.description: Account the launcher uses when neither --account nor CLAUDE_RO_ACCOUNT is set. Must be present in accounts[] once set. Empty string is valid before the first provision_account (and for GitHub/Mongo-only setups).

accounts.description: One entry per AWS account the user has bound. Each holds its own RO role and clusters[]. Empty before the first provision_account (and for GitHub/Mongo-only setups).

ro_role_name.description: Generated at provision time as claude-ro-<short_uuid> (8 hex). Avoids collision with any pre-existing claude-ro role.

assumer_profile.description: Name of the user's AWS CLI profile that has working creds in this account. Required --aws-profile flag on provision-account; reused from this record by deprovision-account / bind-cluster / unbind-cluster.

trust_principal_arn.description: Captured from `aws sts get-caller-identity` at provision time. v1 supports IAM-user principals only.

trust_principal_kind.description: v1 supports only iam_user. Phase 2 may add sso_role / federated.

clusters.description: Bound k8s clusters within this account. Empty until bind-cluster is run for the first cluster.

ca_data.description: Base64-encoded PEM. Embedded into per-launch kubeconfig.

access_entry_principal_arn.description: Should equal accounts[].ro_role_arn — recorded for audit.

supplemental_cluster_role.description: Name of the per-cluster ClusterRole that grants get/list/watch on enumerated CRDs. Aggregated to view.

s3_decrypt_grants.description: Per-bucket holes punched in the guardrails' kms:Decrypt deny by grant-s3-decrypt. Each entry both narrows the DenyKmsDecrypt statement (a negated condition on the S3 encryption context) and adds its own scoped Allow — ReadOnlyAccess carries no kms:Decrypt, so narrowing the deny alone grants nothing. Empty/absent means kms:Decrypt is denied outright, the v1 behavior.

prefix.description: Object-key prefix, or null for bucket-wide. Only expressible when bucket_key_enabled is false: with bucket keys on, S3 puts the BUCKET arn in the encryption context, so there is nothing sub-bucket to match.

region.description: The bucket's region. Pins kms:ViaService on the Allow.

kms_key_arn.description: Resolved key ARN. Alias ARNs are not valid in an IAM Resource, so alias/aws/s3 is resolved through kms:DescribeKey at grant time.

bucket_key_enabled.description: Read from the bucket's default encryption at grant time. Decides whether the encryption context is the bucket ARN or the object ARN.

encryption_context.description: The aws:s3:arn value this grant matches: a bucket ARN (context_match=equals) or an object-ARN pattern ending in * (context_match=like).

verify_fixtures.description: Deterministic identifiers for shared verification fixtures inside this account / its clusters. Names are derived from account_id (where the namespace is global, e.g. S3 bucket / KMS alias) or fixed (where it's account-scoped). Created by ensure_verify_fixtures(account_id, region) which is idempotent: provider 'already exists' errors (BucketAlreadyOwnedByYou, ResourceExistsException, etc.) are treated as success. Fixtures are ORG-SHARED — many engineers in one account reuse the same set. deprovision-account does NOT delete them; use `revoke purge-org-fixtures <account_id> --confirm` when no engineer in the org is using the account anymore. This object is therefore a deterministic cache: the names are stable for the lifetime of the account binding, even across re-provisions.

verify_bucket.description: S3 bucket name. Format: claude-ro-verify-<account_id> (S3 namespace is global, must include account ID).

verify_secret_id.description: Secrets Manager secret name. Format: claude-ro-verify-deny (account-scoped).

verify_kms_key_id.description: KMS key ID. The aliased name `alias/claude-ro-verify` is account-scoped; the underlying KeyId is recorded here for the verify call.

verify_glacier_key.description: S3 object key inside verify_bucket whose storage-class is GLACIER, used for the s3:RestoreObject deny check. Account-scoped within the bucket.

verify_pods.description: Map cluster_name -> pod name in default namespace. Format: claude-ro-verify-deny (cluster-scoped).

verify_crd_kind.description: Map cluster_name -> one CRD kind sampled at provision time. Used by verify to confirm the supplemental ClusterRole landed.

github.description: One entry per org the user has bound: a read-only GitHub App OWNED BY that org and installed on it (private — owner == install target). ALL bound orgs are reachable at once in claude-ro via the shared claude-ro-mint-github broker (no per-launch selection). Added at schema v2.

login.description: The org/user login this App is owned by + installed on; also the runtime/github/<login>.token filename.

account_type.description: Whether `login` is an organization or a personal user account (routes the App create page + delete URL).

installation_id.description: The App's installation on its org.

secret_ref.description: Filename (not path) of the mode-600 App private-key PEM under the secrets dir. Never the key itself.

mongodb.description: Top-level MongoDB deployments the user has bound (independent of accounts[]). ALL bound DBs are reachable at once in claude-ro via the shared claude-ro-mint-mongodb broker (no per-launch selection). The read-only DB user is created by the DB owner out of band; only its password is stored (in the secret file). Added at schema v2.

name.description: Identifier for this DB; also the MONGODB_URI_<NAME> env-var suffix (upper-cased, -/. → _). Same charset restriction as github[].name.

kind.description: Only picks the URI form (srv host vs host list) and verify reachability expectations.

auth.description: Authentication method. Absent/`password` (default): a stored RO-user password (username + secret_ref). `aws_iam` (Atlas only): the DB user is claude-ro's per-account RO role (iam_role_arn) and connections use MONGODB-AWS with claude-ro's minted RO creds — no password, no stored secret.

aws_account_id.description: aws_iam only: which provisioned account's RO role authenticates to this Atlas DB (its minted creds are used at connect time).

iam_role_arn.description: aws_iam only: the RO role ARN registered as the Atlas DB user (accounts[].ro_role_arn for aws_account_id, captured at bind time so a re-provision churn is visible).

srv.description: true → mongodb+srv:// using srv_host; false → mongodb:// using hosts.

srv_host.description: Present when srv is true, e.g. prod-0.ab12.mongodb.net.

hosts.description: Present when srv is false, e.g. n1:27017,n2:27017.

username.description: password auth: the read-only DB user, e.g. claude-ro-<engineer>. Absent for aws_iam.

via_cluster.description: Optional: kubectl context (in the ENGINEER's kubeconfig) of a cluster with network line-of-sight to this DB. When set, claude-ro stands up a per-session SOCKS5 proxy on demand via the engineer-run claude-ro-tunnel-<cluster> broker; the tunnel's local port is chosen per session at run time (NOT stored here) and the agent passes it to the Mongo minter, which bakes proxyHost/proxyPort into the URI. Engineer-side only — claude-ro's RO role never touches the cluster.

secret_ref.description: password auth only (absent for aws_iam): filename (not path) of the mode-600 file holding the RO user's password.

snowflake.description: Top-level Snowflake accounts the user has bound (independent of accounts[]). ALL bound Snowflake identities are reachable at once in claude-ro via the shared claude-ro-mint-snowflake broker (no per-launch selection). Auth is RSA key-pair: the durable private key PEM lives mode-600 under the secrets dir and the broker signs a short-lived JWT with it, so no long-lived credential ever enters the sandbox. The read-only service user + role are created by the Snowflake account admin out of band; only the private key is stored.

name.description: Identifier for this Snowflake binding; also the SNOWFLAKE_*_<NAME> env-var suffix (upper-cased, -/. → _). Same charset restriction as mongodb[].name.

account.description: The ORG-QUALIFIED account identifier as it appears in the Snowsight URL (e.g. kpsovyc-ta51714) — this is what routes to the account's endpoint. Deliberately NOT what CURRENT_ACCOUNT() returns: that is the account LOCATOR, which does not route, and pasting it here yields a connection that never resolves.

service_user.description: The read-only Snowflake service user the key is registered on (e.g. CLAUDE_RO_<ENGINEER>), created out of band by the account admin. Stored unqualified for display and for the admin-side ALTER USER statements.

qualified_username.description: <ACCOUNT>.<SERVICE_USER>, upper-cased, computed at bind time. Used verbatim as the JWT `sub` (and as the `iss` prefix). Recorded rather than re-derived per mint so a wrong account/user pairing surfaces once, at bind, instead of as an opaque JWT rejection every hour inside the broker.

public_key_fp.description: SHA256:… fingerprint of the registered public key, read back from DESCRIBE USER at bind time. Forms the JWT `iss` (<qualified_username>.<fp>). Pinned here for the same reason as qualified_username: a key that was never registered, or was rotated out from under us, fails loudly at bind rather than silently every hour in the broker.

role.description: The read-only role the broker requests at connect time (e.g. READ_ALL). The grant itself lives in Snowflake; this only selects which of the user's granted roles is activated, so a broadened grant cannot silently widen the session.

warehouse.description: Optional: default warehouse for the session (e.g. COMPUTE_WH). Absent means the user's own DEFAULT_WAREHOUSE applies; queries fail with 'no warehouse selected' if neither is set.

database.description: Optional: default database for the session. Purely a convenience for unqualified queries — it grants nothing the role does not already have.

secret_ref.description: Filename (not path) of the mode-600 RSA private-key PEM under the secrets dir. Never the key itself, and never a path — the secrets dir is resolved by the broker so state.json cannot be edited to point the reader at an arbitrary file.

lockdown.description: Filename-only Tier 2 classifier state. Filename + path are the only signals; no content is read or sent. Verdicts are 'sensitive' or 'not_sensitive' only — fail-safe coercion in apply ensures any malformed verdict becomes 'sensitive'.

classifier_cache.description: Map absolute path -> verdict. Filename-only classification is a pure function of the path; mtime/size are deliberately not part of the key (a `touch` should not invalidate the verdict).

extensions.description: Reserved for the Phase 2 extension flow. Always empty in v1; Skill 3 must read the schema correctly so v2 doesn't break teardown.

pending_operation.description: Set by the orchestrator at the start of a mutating sub-command, cleared after the final state_commit + verify pass. Drives partial-failure resume.

target.description: Op-specific target; e.g. {account_id, cluster_name} for bind-cluster.

last_completed_phase.description: null right after begin_operation (no phase completed yet), then the name of the last completed phase.
